title: Every hop needs its own bound, and the cheapest place to say no is the edge
caption: Each arrow is a place where work can pile up, so each one gets a limit and a policy for when it's reached.

steps.text: Edge: admission control. A token bucket or waiting-room token decides who gets in; a 429 here costs microseconds.
Service: bounded concurrency, e.g. at most 200 requests in flight per instance. Request 201 gets a fast 503 instead of queueing in memory.
Queue: a maximum depth. When it's full, the service rejects or waits briefly, so the queue can't grow without limit.
Workers pull, so they can't be overrun. If they fall behind, the queue's lag grows, and lag is the metric you alert on.
Database: a connection pool of 20. Extra work waits for a connection, with a deadline, instead of opening the 500th connection.

scenarios.name: Database slows down
scenarios.summary: A slow database is felt hop by hop backwards: the pool, then the queue, then the service, until the edge starts saying no, and every hop stays within its limit.

steps.text: The database slows down. All 20 pool connections are busy, and new work waits for one, until its deadline.
Workers finish fewer jobs, so they pull less. The queue's lag grows until it reaches its maximum depth.
The full queue makes the service reject or briefly wait. Its in-flight count climbs to the cap, and extra requests get a fast 503.
The edge sees the 503s and sheds early with 429 + Retry-After. The system is slower, but nothing has run out of memory.

scenarios.name: Risk: a hop with no bound
scenarios.summary: One unbounded hop undoes the rest: an unlimited connection count turns a slow database into a dead one.

steps.text: Every other hop has its limit, but workers open a new database connection per job, with no pool.
When the database slows down, jobs take longer, so more run at once and more connections open: 20, 200, 2 000.
The database spends its memory and CPU on connections instead of queries, slows further, and finally refuses everyone.
Mitigation: a fixed pool with a wait deadline. Excess work waits upstream, in the bounded queue, where it's cheap.
